You're working on Nxeon, a hosting platform (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres). `/opt/nxeon` is production (git, origin/main). `/opt/nxeon-staging` is a separate staging checkout with its own DB, used for verification before anything touches prod.

## The bug, confirmed by a real screenshot from the owner

The "Add funds" flow on the Billing page (`/dashboard/billing`) is visually broken. The owner clicked "Add $25" (or similar) and got a tiny, badly-laid-out popup: a small box reading "Add $25.00 to your wallet" with "Nxeon wallet credit" and "US$25.00" text overlapping/cut off inside an undersized white box, layered oddly on top of the page. It's unusable.

## The fix — don't patch the broken popup, replace it

The owner's explicit ask: "lets turn this into a popup with similar payment ui to the deploy wizard." Find the current add-funds flow (grep the Billing page — likely `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` and a client component it renders, maybe something like `components/customer/AddFundsModal.tsx` or inline in a `WalletControls`-type component — read the actual current implementation first, don't guess the filename) and replace its payment UI with the SAME real, working pattern used everywhere else in this app today: `components/customer/PaymentStep.tsx`, a real embedded Stripe Custom Checkout (`ui_mode: "elements"`), the same component that powers the VPS/Hosting/Game/Email deploy wizards' Review step.

Read these reference files fully before writing anything:
- `components/customer/PaymentStep.tsx` — the actual payment UI component (card + Google/Apple Pay via one combined `ExpressCheckoutElement`, the Geist-font-fixed Stripe Elements styling, the billing-term/order-summary panel). For an add-funds flow you likely only need a SIMPLIFIED version of what it renders (there's no "order summary" or "billing term" for a wallet top-up — just an amount and a pay button) — check whether `PaymentStep` already supports a minimal/no-order-summary mode, or whether the cleanest approach is a smaller sibling component that reuses the same underlying `<PaymentElement>`/`<ExpressCheckoutElement>` setup and Stripe Elements options (`STRIPE_APPEARANCE`, `STRIPE_FONTS`) but with its own simpler layout. Use your judgment on which is less invasive, but the visual/interaction quality must match — this is explicitly what "similar payment ui to the deploy wizard" means.
- `lib/stripe.ts` — find the actual server-side function that creates a Stripe session for a wallet top-up specifically (search for "top-up", "topup", or wherever `creditCheckoutSession`/`creditExternalPayment` get their session from — there's a `createOrderPaymentSession`-style function for orders; there should be an equivalent for a plain top-up, or the current broken popup calls something else entirely that needs to be swapped to the Custom Checkout (`ui_mode: "elements"`) pattern instead of whatever embedded/old pattern it currently uses). Confirm it already sets `saved_payment_method_options: { payment_method_save: "enabled" }` (a real bug fixed earlier today across the 4 product session-builders — check whether the top-up one has it; if not, this is the same fix, add it).
- Whatever the CURRENT add-funds component is — read it fully to understand the exact broken markup/CSS causing the tiny overlapping box, so you understand what's being replaced and don't leave any dead code behind.

## Scope
- This should become a real popup/modal (the owner's word), not a full-page navigation — matching how PaymentStep is typically presented within a step of a wizard, but here it's a standalone modal triggered from the Billing page's existing "Add funds" button/quick-amount buttons ($25/$100/$5 chips visible in the current UI, keep those as the amount-selection entry point).
- Preserve the existing amount-selection UI (the quick-amount buttons/custom amount input) — only the PAYMENT step (the part that's currently broken) needs to become the new, working, well-styled popup.
- On successful payment, the wallet balance should update and the modal should close/show success — check how the deploy wizards handle their own post-payment success state for the pattern to mirror (though a full ProvisioningOverlay-style animation is overkill for a simple top-up — a simple success state/toast within the modal is enough, use your judgment).

## Verification discipline
1. Baseline: `cd /opt/nxeon && npm test 2>&1 | grep "^not ok"` before changes (34 pre-existing failures expected, all pricing/proration/auth-flavored).
2. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after.
3. `npm test` failure set identical to baseline after.
4. Commit ending in:
   ```

   Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   ```
   `git push origin main` — retry once after 2s on "cannot lock ref" (transient, known issue, other work lands on main concurrently from elsewhere in this session).
5. Deploy to staging: `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (may background-timeout the calling shell call — check its output file rather than re-running).
6. Verify LIVE on staging with Playwright (`/opt/nxeon-staging/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs`, `chromium.launch()` + `newContext({ bypassCSP: true })`, login `claude-audit-2026@nxeon.test` / `AuditPass123!` at `https://staging.nxeon.cloud`): go to `/dashboard/billing`, click Add Funds, pick an amount, confirm the new popup renders correctly (real Stripe card fields, no overlapping/cut-off text, matches the deploy wizard's visual quality), and run an actual test-mode payment through to completion (Stripe test card `4242424242424242`, `12/34`, `123` — the exact pattern used throughout this session's other test scripts, e.g. `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/audit.mjs` if you want a reference for the iframe-filling pattern) and confirm the wallet balance actually increased afterward via a direct Prisma query. Take screenshots.

## Hard constraints
- Do **NOT** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` — staging only, the owner reviews before promoting.
- Don't run `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon` itself.
- Don't scope-creep — only fix the add-funds popup. Note anything else you notice in your final report instead of fixing it inline.

## Final report
What the old broken component looked like and why it broke, what you replaced it with, verification results (tsc/test-diff, staging deploy, the real test payment and confirmed wallet balance increase, screenshots), and any judgment calls.
